brief: GS flow note on yesterday's violent US equity liquidation (SPX down 3.3% intraday, breadth 38 advancing against 464 declining, negative gamma into expiry), framed as catalysts meant to be supportive instead triggering a selloff. New BIS export rules effective Nov 19 close the offshore-compute loophole, restricting China's direct chip access, remote compute access and foundry capacity. The immediate risk is licensing uncertainty freezing investment decisions, not permanent demand loss, tied to weak Asian data center trades and Shanghai testing its lows, with possible spillover into copper and gold. Compounding multiple compression: cost of capital, worsened by Nvidia's leadership change, inference oversupply and efficiency gains, and thin capex revenue. Defensive sectors failed to hold absolute ground despite some Treasury yield relief. Macro thread: financial conditions have tightened sharply, hawkish Fed speakers including Waller's 50bp remarks echo a 2018 overtightening parallel. Collapsing breakevens have pushed real yields toward relative highs even as growth and liquidity deteriorate, and the long end may be starting to price a policy mistake. The author favors receiving rates and owning duration, watches gold as a coincident indicator, and reads deep de-grossing as a possible tactical local low ahead of PCE, NFP, the December FOMC and November CPI.
